test_cases.title: rebuild_program_rollups fully replaces all 7 program-scoped rollup tables from usage_events alone
test_cases.given: usage_events holds rows for program P across multiple sessions, commands, and releases
test_cases.then: every program-scoped rollup table is fully replaced with values derived solely from usage_events rows for P
test_cases.objective: Verify rebuild_program_rollups derives correct aggregate values for all 7 program-scoped tables from usage_events alone, with no other data source.
preconditions: Disposable test database migrated to head (18-table BED-01 schema)
usage_events seeded with a representative set of rows for program_id='prog-test-1': 3 sessions, 5 distinct commands, 2 releases, token usage on each row
steps: Seed usage_events with test_data.seeded_event_count rows for program_id='prog-test-1', spanning known sessions/commands/releases/token counts
Call await rebuild_program_rollups(session, 'prog-test-1')
Query each of the 7 tables in test_data.tables filtered to program_id='prog-test-1'
expected_results: All 7 tables contain rows for prog-test-1
Each table's aggregate values (counts, sums, series points) match hand-computed expectations derived directly from the seeded usage_events rows
Returned RebuildResult.event_count == 12 and RebuildResult.scope == 'program'

test_cases.title: Program-scoped rebuild deletes stale rows for events removed since the prior rebuild (DELETE+INSERT, not UPDATE/upsert)
test_cases.given: rebuild_program_rollups(P) has already run once, producing rollup rows anchored to an initial usage_events set
test_cases.when: a subset of P's usage_events rows is removed (simulating a corrected batch) and rebuild_program_rollups(P) runs again
test_cases.then: the rollup rows attributable only to the removed events are gone, not left behind as stale patched rows, proving the mechanism is DELETE...WHERE program_id=:pid + INSERT, never UPDATE/ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE
test_cases.objective: Prove FR-2's full-replace mechanics: a second rebuild after data shrinks removes stale aggregate contributions rather than leaving an incremental patch behind.
preconditions: Disposable test database migrated to head
usage_events seeded with 10 rows for program_id='prog-test-2' including one distinct command 'rare-cmd' used only in 2 of those rows
steps: Seed usage_events (10 rows) for prog-test-2 including 2 rows with cmd_name='rare-cmd'
Call rebuild_program_rollups(session, 'prog-test-2') and confirm program_commands contains a 'rare-cmd' row
Delete the 2 usage_events rows matching test_data.removed_event_filter directly from usage_events
Call rebuild_program_rollups(session, 'prog-test-2') again
expected_results: After the second rebuild, program_commands no longer contains a 'rare-cmd' row for prog-test-2
Remaining program-scoped rollup rows reflect only the 8 surviving usage_events rows
No row in any of the 7 program-scoped tables reflects the deleted events

test_cases.title: rebuild_org_rollups fully replaces all 3 org-scoped rollup tables from usage_events across all programs
test_cases.given: usage_events holds rows across 3 distinct programs
test_cases.then: every org-scoped rollup table is fully replaced with values derived from usage_events across all programs
test_cases.objective: Verify rebuild_org_rollups derives correct aggregate values for all 3 org-scoped tables from the full usage_events set.
preconditions: Disposable test database migrated to head
usage_events seeded with rows across program_id in {'prog-a','prog-b','prog-c'}, distinct token totals and active users per program
steps: Seed usage_events with test_data.seeded_event_count rows spread across test_data.program_ids
Call await rebuild_org_rollups(session)
Query each of the 3 tables in test_data.tables
expected_results: All 3 org-scoped tables contain rows reflecting all 3 programs combined
Aggregate values match hand-computed expectations summed/derived across all seeded usage_events rows
Returned RebuildResult.event_count == 30, scope == 'org', program_id is None

test_cases.title: Org-scoped rebuild deletes stale rows for a program's events removed since the prior rebuild
test_cases.given: rebuild_org_rollups() has already run once with events present for program 'prog-b'
test_cases.when: all of prog-b's usage_events rows are removed and rebuild_org_rollups() runs again
test_cases.then: prog-b's contribution is fully removed from the org-scoped tables' aggregates, not left as a stale patched value
test_cases.objective: Prove FR-2's full-replace mechanics at org scope: a second rebuild after a program's events disappear removes that program's aggregate contribution entirely.
preconditions: Disposable test database migrated to head
usage_events seeded across prog-a and prog-b, with prog-b contributing a known distinct token total
steps: Seed usage_events for prog-a and prog-b
Call rebuild_org_rollups(session) and record org_summary_rollup / token_series aggregate values
Delete all usage_events rows where program_id='prog-b'
Call rebuild_org_rollups(session) again
expected_results: Second-run org_summary_rollup / token_series / mau_series values equal exactly prog-a's contribution alone
No trace of prog-b's prior contribution remains in any org-scoped table

test_cases.title: Rebuild run twice on an unchanged event set produces byte-identical rollup rows
test_cases.given: usage_events holds a fixed set of rows for program P and rebuild_program_rollups(P) has already been run once
test_cases.when: rebuild_program_rollups(P) is invoked a second time with no change to usage_events
test_cases.then: the second run's rollup rows are byte-identical to the first run's, across all 7 program-scoped tables
test_cases.objective: Verify idempotency: re-running the rebuild against an unchanged event set is a no-op with respect to observable output.
preconditions: Disposable test database migrated to head
usage_events seeded with 8 rows for program_id='prog-idem-1'
steps: Seed usage_events for prog-idem-1
Call rebuild_program_rollups(session, 'prog-idem-1') and snapshot a row-checksum + COUNT(*) per program-scoped table
Call rebuild_program_rollups(session, 'prog-idem-1') again with no intervening writes
Snapshot the same checksum + COUNT(*) per table
expected_results: Second snapshot's checksum and COUNT(*) are identical to the first snapshot, for all 7 tables
No duplicate or drifted rows appear after the second run

test_cases.title: Duplicate ingest payload is rejected by the unique constraint and the second rebuild is identical to the first (FR-4 mechanics)
test_cases.given: an ingest write posts a usage_events payload once, rebuild runs, then the identical payload is posted a second time
test_cases.when: the second identical insert is attempted against usage_events and the second rebuild runs
test_cases.then: the duplicate insert raises a unique-constraint violation on (program_id, session_id, cmd_ts) rather than being silently accepted, and the rollup rows after the second rebuild are byte-identical to the first run — no double-counting
test_cases.objective: Verify the exact idempotency test mechanics specified in FR-4: seed, rebuild, snapshot, attempt duplicate insert (assert UniqueViolation), rebuild again, assert byte-identical second snapshot.
preconditions: Disposable test database migrated to head
usage_events has the unique constraint on (program_id, session_id, cmd_ts) from BED-01's migration
steps: Insert test_data.payload_row_count usage_events rows for prog-idem-2 (one row keyed on session_id='sess-1', cmd_ts=test_data.cmd_ts)
Call rebuild_program_rollups(session, 'prog-idem-2') and snapshot per-table checksum + COUNT(*)
Attempt to re-insert the identical row (program_id='prog-idem-2', session_id='sess-1', cmd_ts=test_data.cmd_ts) into usage_events
Call rebuild_program_rollups(session, 'prog-idem-2') again
Snapshot per-table checksum + COUNT(*) a second time
expected_results: The duplicate insert attempt raises a unique-constraint violation (asyncpg.UniqueViolationError / IntegrityError) on (program_id, session_id, cmd_ts)
usage_events row count for prog-idem-2 remains test_data.payload_row_count after the failed duplicate insert
Second rebuild's snapshot is byte-identical to the first snapshot across all 7 program-scoped tables

test_cases.title: rebuild_program_rollups(P) changes only program P's rollup rows
test_cases.given: usage_events holds rows for program P and unrelated program Q
test_cases.then: only program P's rollup rows change; program Q's rollup rows are untouched
test_cases.objective: Verify the rebuild is scoped strictly to the target program and never performs a global scan or write.
preconditions: Disposable test database migrated to head
usage_events seeded for program_id='prog-p' and program_id='prog-q'
Both programs' rollup tables pre-populated via an initial rebuild_program_rollups call for each
steps: Rebuild both prog-p and prog-q once, snapshot prog-q's row checksums across all 7 program-scoped tables
Add 3 new usage_events rows for prog-p only
Call rebuild_program_rollups(session, 'prog-p')
Re-snapshot prog-q's row checksums across all 7 program-scoped tables
expected_results: prog-p's rollup rows reflect the 3 newly added events
prog-q's row checksums after the rebuild are identical to the pre-rebuild snapshot — zero rows changed

test_cases.title: Program-scope isolation holds under a wide fan-out of unrelated programs
test_cases.given: usage_events holds rows for 10 distinct programs
test_cases.when: rebuild_program_rollups is called for exactly one of the 10 programs
test_cases.then: the other 9 programs' rollup rows remain byte-identical, confirming O(events for P) scoping rather than any cross-program leakage even at higher program cardinality
test_cases.objective: Extend the isolation guarantee to a higher-cardinality scenario, closing the boundary case a 2-program test could miss (e.g. an unfiltered WHERE clause that happens to work with only 2 rows present).
preconditions: Disposable test database migrated to head
usage_events seeded for 10 distinct program_ids, each already rebuilt once
steps: Snapshot row checksums for all 7 program-scoped tables across all 10 programs
Add usage_events rows for prog-05 only
Call rebuild_program_rollups(session, 'prog-05')
Re-snapshot checksums for the remaining 9 programs
expected_results: prog-05's rows reflect the new events
All 9 other programs' checksums are unchanged across all 7 tables

test_cases.title: rollup_rebuild.py exports the documented signatures, RebuildResult shape, and never constructs its own session
test_cases.when: the module's public exports are inspected via reflection and a call is made with an injected AsyncSession
test_cases.then: rebuild_program_rollups(session, program_id) and rebuild_org_rollups(session) exist with the documented async signatures, return a RebuildResult carrying scope/program_id/duration_ms/event_count, and neither function creates its own session/engine internally
test_cases.objective: Verify FR-1's contract: exact module path, function signatures, DI mechanism, and the settlement of the stale backend/app/services/ingest.py test-mapping path.
preconditions: services/api/app/services/rollup_rebuild.py importable
app/core/db.py's get_db()/SessionLocal importable
steps: Import rebuild_program_rollups and rebuild_org_rollups from app.services.rollup_rebuild
Inspect each function's signature via inspect.signature() and confirm parameter names/types (session: AsyncSession, program_id: str for the program variant)
Call rebuild_program_rollups(injected_session, 'prog-x') against a seeded test DB and inspect the returned object
Scan rollup_rebuild.py source for any direct SessionLocal()/create_async_engine() call inside the two functions
expected_results: Both functions are coroutine functions with the documented parameter signatures
The returned object exposes exactly test_data.expected_result_fields with correct types (scope: 'program', program_id: str, duration_ms: int, event_count: int)
Neither function constructs its own session — the injected session is the only session used

test_cases.title: A failure mid-rebuild rolls back the entire transaction — no partial rebuild visible to a concurrent reader
test_cases.given: rebuild_program_rollups(P) is mid-transaction, having already deleted and re-inserted rows for some of the 7 program-scoped tables
test_cases.when: an exception is forced during the INSERT for one of the remaining tables (e.g. a monkeypatched write raising an IntegrityError)
test_cases.then: the entire async with session.begin() block rolls back — none of the 7 tables show any change, matching their pre-rebuild state exactly
test_cases.objective: Verify the top research risk (transaction atomicity): all 7 (or 3) table mutations for one rebuild call commit or roll back together, never partially, per FR-2's single-transaction requirement.
preconditions: Disposable test database migrated to head
usage_events seeded for program_id='prog-atomic-1' with an existing prior rollup state from a first successful rebuild
steps: Rebuild prog-atomic-1 once and snapshot checksums for all 7 tables
Add new usage_events rows for prog-atomic-1
Monkeypatch/mock the INSERT for test_data.forced_failure_table to raise an exception mid-transaction
Call rebuild_program_rollups(session, 'prog-atomic-1') and expect it to propagate the exception
Re-snapshot checksums for all 7 tables
expected_results: rebuild_program_rollups raises the forced exception rather than swallowing it
All 7 tables' checksums after the failed call exactly match the pre-call snapshot — no partial DELETE/INSERT from any table is visible
A subsequent successful rebuild_program_rollups(P) call (without the forced failure) produces the correct full replacement

test_cases.then: exactly one structured JSON log line named rollup_rebuild_completed is emitted, with scope='program', program_id=P, duration_ms as an int, and event_count matching the scanned usage_events row count
test_cases.objective: Verify FR-5's observability event schema and single-emission point for the program scope, closing research condition C-5.
